binders: A measurable type Omega and a probability measure mu on it.
hypotheses: X is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to mu.
conclusions: At every real t, the pushforward law of X assigns to (-infinity,t] exactly mu{omega | X(omega)<=t}.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef002 is the pushforward Measure.map X mu.
LocalDef001 is that law evaluated on Set.Iic t.
Set.Iic t is the inclusive lower interval.
Its preimage is the event X<=t.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For an almost-everywhere measurable real random variable on a probability space, its pushforward distribution at (-infinity,t] is exactly the probability that X is at most t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The probability assumption is stronger than the raw pushforward identity requires but supplies the intended CDF setting.
The statement concerns inclusive lower intervals and ENNReal-valued probabilities.
The hypotheses are satisfiable and nonvacuous.
